claims.statement: Tom Allen had a home in St. Louis, which he left some months before the Goss fight to go into training.
claims.excerpt: left his home in this city some few months ago, to go into training prior to meeting the English-man Goss

claims.statement: Tom Allen was described as the champion of the prize ring.
claims.excerpt: Tom Allen, the champion of the prize ring

claims.statement: Tom Allen returned to St. Louis by train from Cincinnati on 1876-09-21.
claims.excerpt: This morning the train from Cincinna i brought in the man who had whipped Joe Goss

claims.statement: After arriving in St. Louis, Tom Allen went to Tom Kelly's saloon at No. 9 North Ninth street and shook hands with Kelly.
claims.excerpt: the saloon of Tom _ Kelly, No. 9 North Ninth street
places: No. 9 North Ninth street, St. Louis

claims.statement: Tom Allen was cheated out of the stakes of the Goss fight by a preconcerted action of a band of ruffians, according to the paper.
claims.excerpt: euchred cut of the stakes by a preconcerted action of a band of ruffians.

claims.statement: Tom Allen said he would never again enter the ring.
claims.excerpt: Allen reiterates his former assertion, never again toenterthe ring.

claims.statement: Tom Allen weighed about 180 pounds after the Goss fight.
claims.excerpt: At present Allen will kick the scales at 180 avoirdupois.

notes: The 'cheated out of the stakes' claim is the paper's account of Allen's view.
